messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired - INCIDENT PDR-4821 - metric=http_5xx_rate threshold=4.5% (3m window) prod-eu-west1 :rotating_light: https://pagerduty.example/PDR-4821

pagerbot: auto-escalation -> on-call (maya). paging now.

maya: acked. I'm on-call, checking dashboards...

alex: on it. pulling logs + traces for /v1/ endpoints

maya: dashboards show 5xx spike concentrated on /v1/stream and /v1/generate, errors mostly 502/504. latency p50/p90 steady, errors correlate with long requests (>1k tokens).

samir: digging into gateway logs, I'm seeing a lot of upstream resets: "upstream connection reset by peer" pointing at runtime-proxy.

jen: any recent infra or proxy changes? checking deploy history...

ops-bot: deploybot: proxy-config-v2 rolled out to hosted-proxies at 02:14 UTC (revision 1234).

alex: that rollout changed keepalive timeout from 30s -> 3s as part of a connection trimming experiment. that seems suspicious for streaming LLM calls.

maya: timeline lines up. long-running streaming requests get their upstream connection closed after ~3s -> 502/504 downstream. customer impact visible for heavy/power users.

samir: here's a short log excerpt showing the failure mode:
```
[2025-08-12T02:18:02Z] runtime-proxy error: upstream reset while writing to downstream (keepalive timeout)
[2025-08-12T02:18:02Z] connection closed by peer after 2.8s, request-id=abc-123, path=/v1/stream
```

alex: mitigation options (fast):
- rollback proxy-config-v2 -> v1 (previous stable)
- increase keepalive timeout to 60s in proxy config (temporary)
- route heavy/long sessions to dedicated inference pool for eu region as fallback

maya: starting rollback now. running: 
```
kubectl -n gateways rollout undo deployment/proxy-deploy --to-revision=1233
```

jen: I'll prepare a traffic shift rule to reduce pressure on eu-west1 for large sessions:
```
routectl set-weight /v1/stream prod-eu-west1=50,dedicated-pool=50 --dry-run && routectl apply
```

ops-bot: rollback job started (job id x782).

incident-bot: PagerDuty note: rollback initiated by maya.

maya: rollback complete. proxy-deploy back to v1, 8/8 pods ready.

alex: applying keepalive bump to 60s in config map now.

samir: monitoring logs: no upstream resets in the last 2 minutes for long requests.

maya: metrics: 5xx rate (stream endpoints, eu-west1) -> 11% at peak, now down to ~1.2% over the last 3m. :thumbsup:

jen: traffic shift applied to dedicated-pool for heavy sessions, canary 50/50 for 15m.

alex: leaving canary and monitoring for 30m. alert thresholds temporarily lowered to catch regressions.

maya: customer impact summary: a minority of heavy users saw truncated/failed streams during the 15m window after the rollout. No full-account outages. recommend a short incident notice if we hear from customers.

samir: agreed. prepare a single-line customer guidance: "If you experienced truncated responses between 02:14-02:30 UTC in eu-west1, we identified and rolled back a proxy config change; normal behavior has resumed."

maya: noted. I'll draft and share with comms.

jen: followups (postmortem items):
- revert keepalive experiment until we have long-stream test coverage
- add automated canary check that fires if 5xx for streaming endpoints > 1%
- add runbook step to detect keepalive-induced resets

maya: handing over active monitoring to alex for the next hour. summary for handoff: keepalive change caused upstream closes on long streaming LLM sessions, rolled back to stable, keepalive increased, traffic shifted to dedicated pool, 5xx back to normal.

alex: ack takeover. I'll keep watching metrics and update if anything regresses.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: PDR-4821 acknowledged by maya.

ops-bot: PagerDuty incident closed (auto) after 42m. incident duration: ~42m.

maya: closing thread here. I'll open a short postmortem doc and link when ready. :white_check_mark:

maya: next actions assigned: alex -> monitoring for 1h, jen -> create postmortem skeleton, samir -> add long-stream test to infra, ops -> add auto-rollback for keepalive-like config changes.

alex: acked. will follow up in postmortem.
